detailed_description: JSON to Dart converts a pasted JSON value into Dart classes in the browser. Enter a class name (default User) and paste JSON into the input textarea, then click Convert. The tool calls JSON.parse and walks the value, generating one Dart class per nested object. Each class has `final` typed fields, a `const` constructor with `required` named parameters, a `fromJson` factory that reads from `Map<String, dynamic>`, and a `toJson` method. Arrays use `List<...>`; lists of objects produce a nested class based on the first item; scalar fields are inferred as `String`, `int`, `double`, `bool`, or `dynamic`. Invalid JSON shows an error and clears the output. The output appears in a read-only textarea (no built-in copy button, no file download). The tool does not pick null safety modes, generate `==`/`hashCode`/`copyWith`, support `json_serializable`/`freezed` annotations, normalize snake_case to camelCase, infer dates or enums, or validate generated code.
usage_steps: Enter a Dart class name in the class name field
Paste a JSON object into the JSON textarea (a small sample is provided)
Click Convert to generate the Dart classes
Read the generated classes with `final` fields, a constructor, fromJson and toJson in the Dart panel
Check the error banner if the input is not valid JSON, then fix and convert again
Select the generated text in the read-only output to copy it into your editor
usage_examples: Generate a User class with fromJson and toJson from a small user JSON object
Convert a nested response into multiple Dart classes, one per nested object
Try a list of items and see the wrapper class plus a nested class for the first item shape
Spot incorrectly typed fields by reviewing the inferred `String`, `int`, `double`, `bool`, or `dynamic` types
